questions.question_text: A purchase agreement is accepted on Thursday evening. By when must the broker deposit the earnest money?
questions.correct_answer: First legal banking day after acceptance
distractors: Within 3 business days of acceptance
Within 24 hours of the signed contract
By the end of the following business week
questions.explanation: Trust money goes into a special trust account at a federally insured financial institution on the first legal banking day after the contract is accepted (SDCL 36-21A-80). A Thursday acceptance means a Friday deposit unless the parties agreed otherwise in writing.

questions.question_text: A broker deposits $200 of personal funds into the trust account to cover monthly bank service fees. Is this permitted?
distractors: Yes, personal funds may cover bank charges
Yes, up to $500 of personal funds is always allowed
Yes, if tracked on a separate broker ledger line
questions.explanation: South Dakota has no bank-charge exception. Keeping the licensee's own money in the same account as funds belonging to others is commingling and unprofessional conduct (SDCL 36-21A-71(5)). Bank fees come out of the brokerage's operating account.

questions.question_text: What type of reconciliation does South Dakota require for trust accounts?
distractors: Annual audit by a CPA
Quarterly bank statement review
Semi-annual balance confirmation
questions.explanation: The trust account must be reconciled to the bank statement, the trust ledger, and the check register at least monthly (SDCL 36-21A-80). That three-way match is what the commission audits against, and skipping it violates the statute.

questions.question_text: Which three records must be reconciled in the monthly trust account review?
questions.correct_answer: Bank statement, trust ledger, and check register
distractors: Bank statement, tax records, and closing files
Trust ledger, MLS records, and agency agreements
Check register, listing agreements, and tax returns
questions.explanation: The bank statement, the trust ledger, and the check register must all agree at least once a month (SDCL 36-21A-80). The broker also keeps a deposit slip naming the principal and an individual ledger sheet for each principal (SDCL 36-21A-82).

questions.question_text: A seller is unable to consummate the sale and the buyer is not at fault. What must the broker do with the buyer's deposit?
questions.correct_answer: Return it to the buyer at once
distractors: Keep the earned commission out of it
Split it between the buyer and seller
Hold it until the seller signs a written release
questions.explanation: When the seller cannot complete the sale through no fault of the buyer, the broker has no right to any part of the deposit even though the commission was earned — it goes back at once (SDCL 36-21A-77). A disputed deposit is handled under SDCL 36-21A-81.

questions.question_text: A real estate transaction falls through and the buyer and seller disagree about who gets the earnest money. How can the broker disburse the funds?
questions.correct_answer: Written agreement of all parties or court order
distractors: The broker decides based on the contract terms
Funds go to the seller automatically after 30 days
The SDREC makes the final disbursement decision
questions.explanation: If an accepted purchase agreement does not close, the broker may release trust funds only on written instructions from all parties to the transaction or by court order (SDCL 36-21A-81). The broker's own read of the contract authorizes nothing.

questions.question_text: How long must a South Dakota broker retain transaction records after the final closing?
distractors: 3 years
5 years
7 years
questions.explanation: Listings, offers to purchase, closing statements, and other transaction records must be kept four years (SDCL 36-21A-74). Deposit slips and trust ledger sheets are held at least four years from the closing of the transaction (SDCL 36-21A-82).

questions.question_text: Trust funds remain in the broker's trust account until the transaction is:
distractors: Approved by the lender
Past the inspection period
Recorded at the county office
questions.explanation: Money stays in trust until the transaction is consummated or terminated, and the broker is not entitled to any of it as compensation until then (SDCL 36-21A-84). Lender approval and recording do not release the funds.

questions.question_text: A buyer believes they are entitled to the earnest money after a seller breaches the contract. The seller disagrees. What should the broker do?
questions.correct_answer: Hold funds until mutual agreement or court order
distractors: Release funds to the buyer since seller breached
Split the funds equally between both parties
Send the funds to the SDREC for resolution
questions.explanation: A broker may not pick a winner. Disputed trust funds stay put until every party signs written instructions or a court orders release (SDCL 36-21A-81). The commission does not decide who is entitled to the earnest money.

questions.question_text: Which documents are included in the 4-year record retention requirement for SD brokers?
questions.correct_answer: Agency agreements, contracts, and closing statements
distractors: Only the final purchase agreement and the deed
Only financial records and all bank statements
Only documents signed by both parties involved
questions.explanation: Everything relating to the transaction is covered — listings, offers to purchase, closing statements, agency agreements, addenda, and the seller's disclosure (SDCL 36-21A-74). The broker also tells the commission which bank holds the trust account and under what name (SDCL 36-21A-82).
